question: In a class, the ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3. What fraction of the class are boys?
hint: For every 2 boys there are 3 girls. How many children make up one such group?
solution: For every 2 boys there are 3 girls, so every group of 2 + 3 = 5 children holds 2 boys. The boys are 2/5 of the class.

A.text: 2/3 compares the boys with the girls, not with the whole class. The class has 2 + 3 = 5 parts.

C.text: 3/5 is the fraction of the class that are girls. The question asks about the boys.

D.text: 3/2 turns the ratio round, and it is more than a whole. A part of the class cannot be bigger than the class.

E.text: 1/2 makes the class half boys, as if there were as many boys as girls. For every 2 boys there are 3 girls.

question: Nina and Omar cycle the same road from the school to the park, each at a steady speed. Nina takes 30 minutes and Omar takes 20 minutes. Nina rides at 12 km an hour. How fast does Omar ride?
hint: How long is the road? Nina rides at 12 km an hour for half an hour.
solution: Nina rides for half an hour at 12 km an hour, so the road is 6 km long. Omar rides those 6 km in 20 minutes, a third of an hour, so in a whole hour he would ride 3 × 6 = 18 km. He rides at 18 km an hour.

A.text: 8 km an hour makes Omar slower than Nina. He takes less time on the same road, so he rides faster.

B.text: 22 adds the 10 minutes Omar saves to Nina's speed. On the same road, a shorter time makes the speed so many times as big, not so much bigger.

C.text: 20 is the number of minutes Omar takes, a number from the question, not his speed.

D.text: 6 km is the length of the road, found on the way. The question asks how fast Omar rides.

question: Tom and Ann walk at steady speeds. In the time Tom walks 3 km, Ann walks 2 km. How far has Ann walked when Tom has walked 12 km?
hint: How many times as far as 3 km is 12 km?
solution: 12 km is 4 times 3 km, so Tom has walked for 4 times as long. In that time Ann walks 4 × 2 = 8 km.

B.text: 18 km gives Ann the longer walk. She walks 2 km while Tom walks 3, so she covers less than he does.

C.text: 7.2 km takes 3/5 of 12 km, as if Tom's 3 km were a share of 5. The 3 and the 2 are what each walks in the same time.

D.text: 4 is how many times Tom walked 3 km. Ann walks 2 km each of those times.

E.text: 4.8 km takes 2/5 of 12 km, as if 12 km were the two walks together. 12 km is Tom's walk alone.

question: A recipe for 6 people uses 9 eggs. How many eggs does the same recipe need for 20 people?
hint: How many eggs do 2 people need?
solution: 6 people need 9 eggs, so 2 people need 3 eggs. 20 people are 10 times 2 people, so they need 10 × 3 = 30 eggs.

A.text: 23 adds 14 eggs for the 14 extra people, but the eggs grow in step with the people, not by the same number.

B.text: 180 multiplies 9 by 20 and never divides by 6: the 9 eggs feed 6 people, not one.

D.text: 3 eggs is what 2 people need, and there are 20 people.

E.text: 27 feeds 18 people with three recipes and leaves out the last 2 people.

question: Two boxes, A and B, hold 56 shells between them. For every 3 shells in box A, there are 4 in box B. How many shells are in box A?
hint: How many equal parts do the 56 shells make altogether?
solution: Box A has 3 parts and box B has 4, so the 56 shells make 7 equal parts of 8 shells each. Box A holds 3 × 8 = 24 shells.

A.text: 42 takes box A as three quarters of all the shells, but 3 to 4 means 3 parts out of 7.

C.text: 32 is the number of shells in box B.

D.text: 8 shells is one part, and box A has 3 parts.

E.text: 28 shares the shells equally and forgets the 3 to 4.

question: In a fish tank, there are 3 gold fish (G) for every 5 silver fish (S), and every fish is gold or silver. There are 20 silver fish. How many fish are in the tank?
hint: How many groups of 5 silver fish are there?
solution: 20 silver fish make 4 groups of 5, so there are 4 groups of 3 gold fish, which is 12. Altogether there are 20 + 12 = 32 fish.

A.text: 50 takes 3 of every 5 fish to be gold, but it is 3 gold for every 5 silver, 8 fish in each group.

B.text: 38 makes the gold fish 2 fewer than the silver ones, 18, but the ratio grows with the groups.

C.text: 12 is only the gold fish; the silver ones are in the tank too.

D.text: 20 is the number of silver fish, copied from the question.

question: Three baskets, A, B and C, hold 90 walnuts in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7. How many more walnuts are in basket C than in basket A?
hint: How many equal parts are there in all three baskets together?
solution: There are 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 equal parts, so each part is 90 ÷ 15 = 6 walnuts. Basket C has 7 - 3 = 4 parts more than basket A, which is 4 × 6 = 24 walnuts.

B.text: 36 counts only the parts of A and C, 10 in all, so a part seems to be 9 walnuts; there are 15 parts.

C.text: 42 is how many walnuts are in basket C, not how many more than in A.

D.text: 4 is the difference in parts, and each part is 6 walnuts.

E.text: 12 is how many more are in B than in A, or in C than in B.

question: Two gear wheels turn together: each time a tooth of the big wheel moves past, one tooth of the small wheel moves past too. The big wheel has 21 teeth and the small wheel has 7. How many turns does the small wheel make while the big wheel makes 6 turns?
hint: How many teeth move past while the big wheel turns 6 times?
solution: 6 turns of the big wheel move 6 × 21 = 126 teeth past. The small wheel turns once for every 7 teeth, so it makes 126 ÷ 7 = 18 turns.

A.text: 2 has the small wheel turning more slowly, but a wheel with fewer teeth turns faster.

B.text: 126 is the number of teeth that move past, not the turns of the small wheel.

C.text: 6 is the number of turns of the big wheel, copied from the question; the small wheel turns more often.

E.text: 9 reads three times as many teeth as three more turns: 6 + 3.

question: A dough is made of flour and sugar only, in the ratio 5 : 2 by weight. A baker has 1000 g of flour and 300 g of sugar and makes as much dough as she can. How many grams of flour are left over?
hint: Which runs out first, the flour or the sugar?
solution: 300 g of sugar is 2 parts, so a part is 150 g and the dough takes 5 × 150 = 750 g of flour. All the flour would need 400 g of sugar, which she does not have. So 1000 - 750 = 250 g of flour are left over.

A.text: 550 takes the sugar as 2/5 of the dough, but it is 2 parts out of 7.

C.text: 700 is 1000 - 300, which takes the sugar away from the flour.

D.text: 0 uses all the flour, but that would need 400 g of sugar, and there are only 300 g.

E.text: 1050 g is the dough she makes, not the flour left over.

question: A flower stall sells only roses (R), tulips (T) and daisies (D). It has 2 roses for every 3 tulips, and 4 tulips for every 5 daisies. There are 30 daisies. How many flowers does the stall have?
hint: Find the tulips first, then the roses.
solution: 30 daisies make 6 groups of 5, so there are 6 × 4 = 24 tulips. 24 tulips make 8 groups of 3, so there are 8 × 2 = 16 roses. Altogether there are 30 + 24 + 16 = 70 flowers.

A.text: 60 joins the ratios into 2 : 3 : 5, but the 3 tulips and the 4 tulips belong to different groups.

B.text: 66 joins the ratios into 2 : 4 : 5, but 2 roses go with 3 tulips, not with 4.

C.text: 87 counts one flower fewer each time, 30, 29 and 28, as if for every meant one fewer.

D.text: 54 counts the tulips and the daisies and leaves out the roses.

question: Two shepherds share their bread with a hunter: one shepherd has 5 loaves and the other has 3. The three of them eat all 8 loaves in equal shares. The hunter pays 8 coins, and each shepherd is paid for the bread he gave the hunter, at the same price. How many coins should the shepherd with 5 loaves get?
hint: Cut every loaf into 3 equal pieces. How many pieces does each person eat?
solution: Cut every loaf into 3 pieces: that makes 24 pieces, 8 for each person. The first shepherd had 15 pieces and ate 8, so he gave the hunter 7. The second had 9, ate 8 and gave 1. So the 8 coins go 7 and 1, and the shepherd with 5 loaves gets 7.

A.text: 5 shares the coins like the loaves, 5 to 3, but he also ate some of his own bread: he gave the hunter 7 of the 8 pieces.

B.text: 4 shares the coins equally, but the two shepherds did not give the hunter the same amount of bread.

D.text: 1 coin is what the shepherd with 3 loaves gets.

E.text: 3 coins is the price of one whole loaf, not what the shepherd is owed.

question: Bag A has 1 red bead for every 2 blue beads. Bag B holds twice as many beads as bag A, with 3 red beads for every 1 blue bead. All the beads are tipped into one box. What is the ratio of red beads to blue beads in the box?
hint: Choose a size for bag A, such as 12 beads, and count.
solution: Take 12 beads in bag A: 4 red and 8 blue. Bag B then has 24 beads: 18 red and 6 blue. The box has 22 red and 14 blue beads, and 22 : 14 = 11 : 7.

B.text: 4 : 3 adds the two ratios part by part, 1 + 3 and 2 + 1, but the bags hold different numbers of beads.

C.text: 7 : 11 gives blue to red, the other way round.

D.text: 11 : 18 compares the red beads with all the beads, not with the blue ones.

E.text: 3 : 1 is bag B alone, but the beads of bag A are in the box too.

question: The grass in a meadow grows at the same rate every day. 24 cows would eat all of it in 10 days, and 14 cows in 20 days. How many cows would eat all of it in 40 days?
hint: 14 cows in 20 days eat more grass than 24 cows in 10 days. Where does the extra grass come from?
solution: Count the grass in cow-days, what one cow eats in a day. 24 cows in 10 days eat 240 cow-days, and 14 cows in 20 days eat 280. The extra 40 grew in the 10 days between, so 4 cow-days of grass grow every day. At the start the meadow holds 240 − 10 × 4 = 200 cow-days. In 40 days it gives 200 + 40 × 4 = 360 cow-days, which 360 ÷ 40 = 9 cows eat.

A.text: 6 shares out the grass of 24 cows in 10 days over 40 days and leaves out the grass that grows meanwhile.

B.text: 28 makes the cows grow with the days, 14 × 40 ÷ 20. More days need fewer cows, not more.

D.text: 14 is the smaller herd from the question. In 40 days even fewer cows are enough.

E.text: 7 shares out the grass of 14 cows in 20 days over 40 days and leaves out the grass that grows after day 20.

question: A jar holds peaches in juice, and all the peaches are under the juice. Kim eats a quarter of the peaches, and the level in the jar falls by a fifth. By what part of the new level will it fall if Kim then eats half of the peaches that are left?
hint: Taking out a quarter of the peaches lowered the level by a fifth. What part of the jar's contents were all the peaches?
solution: A quarter of the peaches took up a fifth of the contents, so all the peaches took up four fifths, and the juice one fifth. After Kim eats a quarter, the jar holds a fifth of juice and three fifths of peaches, four fifths in all. Half of the peaches left is three tenths of the old contents, which is 3/10 ÷ 4/5 = 3/8 of the four fifths now in the jar. So the level falls by 3/8.

A.text: 1/5 repeats the first fall. But now a different number of peaches comes out, and the level is lower.

C.text: 2/5 doubles the first fall because half is twice a quarter. But half of the peaches left is not twice the first quarter, and the level is lower now.

D.text: 1/2 takes half of the peaches as half of the jar's contents. The peaches are only part of what is in the jar.

E.text: 4/5 is the part of the contents that all the peaches took up, found on the way.

question: Mia and Leo ate a jar of jam together. Leo ate 20% fewer spoonfuls than Mia, but his spoon held 100% more jam than hers. What part of the jar did Leo eat?
hint: Compare one of Leo's spoonfuls with one of Mia's, and the number of spoonfuls each ate.
solution: Leo ate 80% as many spoonfuls as Mia, and each of his held twice as much as hers. So he ate 0.8 × 2 = 1.6 times as much jam as Mia. The jar splits 8 : 5 between Leo and Mia, so Leo ate 8/13 of it.

A.text: 5/13 is the part of the jar that Mia ate. The question asks about Leo.

B.text: 8/5 is Leo's jam against Mia's, not against the whole jar. As a part of the jar it is 8/13.

C.text: 9/14 adds the changes, 100% − 20%, as if Leo ate 180% of Mia's jam. The changes multiply: 80% of the spoonfuls times twice the spoon.

E.text: 1/2 would mean they ate the same. Leo's bigger spoon more than makes up for his fewer spoonfuls.
